## claude.ai Datadog
This is an MCP server for Datadog (a software observability platform). Consult Datadog docs if you're unsure about how something works in the platform. Docs for this MCP server can be found at https://docs.datadoghq.com/bits_ai/mcp_server/setup/ This server ships skill guides containing domain-specific guidance, workflows, and best practices that are not visible in tool names or schemas. Before invoking other tools, always perform skill discovery by running both paths in parallel: a direct load with `load_datadog_skill` using a general domain name (e.g. skill_name='datadog/traces'), and a call to `list_datadog_skills` with a fuzzy `query` based on topic keywords — load any clearly matching result from the listing along with the related skills it points to. The exception is a follow-up call in a domain whose skill you have already loaded or confirmed absent this session. If nothing clearly fits, do not load a skill — proceed with the tool descriptions. When the user asks to visualize, chart, or graph data — or when loading a data domain skill (e.g. datadog/traces, datadog/logs, datadog/metrics) — also load datadog/visualizations. Investigation results often benefit from charts.

## claude.ai entire-staging-eu
Entire MCP — an investigation surface over Entire's engineering data: repos and their analytics, git history (commits, files, trees, refs, diffs), the AI checkpoints and sessions behind the code (with transcripts and token accounting), trails (PR-like change proposals), and code search. Reads are curated `*_entire` tools; a small write/ops group covers trail/review/runner/dispatch mutations.

Workflow: when you only have a repo name, path, or URL, call resolve_entire_repo first, then pass the repo it returns to repo-scoped tools. Prefer the aggregation tools (get_entire_repo_overview, get_entire_my_activity) over hand-rolling stats from raw listings.

Querying conventions (shared by every tool):
- Addressing: name a repo by a prefixed path (gh/<owner>/<repo>, et/<project>/<repo>, git/<owner>/<repo>) or a repo ULID. Repo ULIDs are REGION-SCOPED — the same repo has a different ULID per region, so never carry a ULID across regions or sessions; if a tool rejects one, re-resolve with resolve_entire_repo.
- Pagination: every list takes an opaque cursor and returns next_cursor when more remains — exhaust the pages before concluding "that's all".
- Time: since/until are ISO 8601 / RFC3339 bounds; where offered, timeframe is a relative window (last-month, last-3-months, last-6-months).
- Size: reads that can be large (files, diffs, transcripts) honor max_tokens and return next_cursor to continue — raise max_tokens or page rather than assuming truncation is the whole story.

Pitfalls:
- sessions[].tokenUsage on a checkpoint is a PER-CHECKPOINT delta, not a session total — sum across a session's checkpoints, or use get_entire_session for the authoritative total.
- list_entire_checkpoints silently truncates older history; for a branch's COMPLETE checkpoint membership, paginate list_entire_commits and collect the per-commit checkpoint IDs.

Skills: before deep work in a domain, load the matching skill (list_entire_skills / load_entire_skill) — entire/checkpoints-and-sessions and entire/token-analysis before token accounting, … [truncated]

44	## Quick Start
45	
46	```bash
47	# To use Homebrew, first tap:
48	brew tap entireio/tap
49	brew trust entireio/tap
50	
51	# Install stable via Homebrew
52	brew install --cask entire
53	
54	# Or install nightly via Homebrew
55	brew install --cask entire@nightly
56	
57	# Or install stable via install.sh
58	curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash
59	
60	# Or install nightly via install.sh
61	curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash -s -- --channel nightly
62	
63	# Or install stable via Scoop (Windows)
64	scoop bucket add entire https://github.com/entireio/scoop-bucket.git
65	scoop install entire/cli
66	
67	# Or install via Go (development/manual setup)
68	go install github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire@latest
69	
70	# Linux: Add Go binaries to PATH (add to ~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc if not already configured)
71	export PATH="$HOME/go/bin:$PATH"
72	
73	# Enable in your project
74	cd your-project && entire enable
75	
76	# Check status
77	entire status
78	```
79	
80	After the initial setup, use `entire agent` to add or remove agents, `entire configure` to update non-agent settings, and `entire enable` / `entire disable` to toggle Entire on or off.
81	
82	## Release Channels
83	
84	Entire currently ships two release channels:
85	
86	- `stable`: recommended for most users. Stable releases change less often and are the default for Homebrew, Scoop, and `install.sh`.
87	- `nightly`: prerelease builds for users who want the latest changes earlier. Nightlies are published more frequently and may include newer, less-proven changes than stable.
88	
89	How to use each channel:
90

## Quick Start

```bash
# To use Homebrew, first tap:
brew tap entireio/tap
brew trust entireio/tap

# Install stable via Homebrew
brew install --cask entire

# Or install nightly via Homebrew
brew install --cask entire@nightly

# Or install stable via install.sh
curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash

# Or install nightly via install.sh
curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash -s -- --channel nightly

# Or install stable via Scoop (Windows)
scoop bucket add entire https://github.com/entireio/scoop-bucket.git
scoop install entire/cli

# Or install via Go (development/manual setup)
go install github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire@latest

# Linux: Add Go binaries to PATH (add to ~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc if not already configured)
export PATH="$HOME/go/bin:$PATH"

# Enable in your project
cd your-project && entire enable

# Check status
entire status
```

After the initial setup, use `entire agent` to add or remove agents, `entire configure` to update non-agent settings, and `entire enable` / `entire disable` to toggle Entire on or off.

## Release Channels

Entire currently ships two release channels:

- `stable`: recommended for most users. Stable releases change less often and are the default for Homebrew, Scoop, and `install.sh`.
- `nightly`: prerelease builds for users who want the latest changes earlier. Nightlies are published more frequently and may include newer, less-proven changes than stable.

How to use each channel:

- Homebrew (one-time setup): `brew tap entireio/tap && brew trust entireio/tap`
- Homebrew stable: `brew install --cask entire`
- Homebrew nightly: `brew install --cask entire@nightly`
- `install.sh` stable: `curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash`
- `install.sh` nightly: `curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash -s -- --channel nightly`
- Scoop: currently supports `stable` only via `scoop install entire/cli`

## Typical Workflow

### 1. Enable Entire in Your Repository

```
entire enable
```

On a repo that has not been enabled yet, `entire enable` runs the initial enable flow: it creates Entire settings, installs git hooks, and prompts you to choose which agent hooks to install. To enable a specific agent non-interactively, use `entire enable --agent <name>` (for example, `entire enable --agent cursor`).

After setup:

- Use `entire enable` to turn Entire back on if the repo is currently disabled.
- Use `entire agent` to add or remove agents.
- Use `entire configure` to update non-agent settings (telemetry, hooks, checkpoint remote, summary provider).

The hooks capture session data as you work. Checkpoints are created when you or the agent make a git commit. Your code commits stay clean, Entire never creates commits on your active branch. All session metadata is stored on a separate `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch.

### 2. Work with Your AI Agent

Just use one of your AI agents as before. Entire runs in the background, tracking your session:
